value.body: Installs, maintains and repairs equipment at customers' premises — for example medical devices in hospitals, analytical instruments in labs, or machines in factories. Equipment makers and their service partners hire for this role. A typical day involves travelling to sites, finding and fixing faults, and writing up service reports.

items.label: Typical entry
items.value: B.Sc Electronics / Physics, a diploma, or a B.Tech in ECE, EEE or Instrumentation

items.label: Common tools
items.value: Multimeters, oscilloscopes, service manuals and the maker's diagnostic software

items.label: Work pattern
items.value: Regular travel within an assigned territory
items.note: Two-wheeler and driving licence are often asked for

value.title: How you get in
value.body: Freshers usually join as trainee service engineers with an equipment maker or a dealer, and learn specific product lines through company training. Interviews check basic electronics, fault-finding and communication. Willingness to travel and to work in a given city or region is usually a condition.

value.title: Skills you'll use
items: Reading circuit diagrams and service manuals

value.title: At a glance
items: Growth path: service engineer → senior / specialist engineer → service or regional manager.
Product knowledge built on the job can lead to application or sales roles.
Travel, on-call duty and site deadlines are common.
